title: libpod: release pod lock before sdnotify healthy wait
body:
Container.Start() holds the pod lock via a defer until it returns. When a container is started with the --sdnotify=healthy flag, it waits to become healthy while holding the pod lock, which blocks operations that require the lock, such as pod inspect and create --pod.

Replace the deferred unlock in Container.Start() with a once-only closure (releasePodLock) called before the health wait. Start() passes this closure to startNoPodLockWithCallback, while startNoPodLock itself passes nil and remains unchanged.

Add a BATS test verifying the fix. Tested locally with pod inspect, create --pod, and a race check where pod stop successfully finished during the background start's health wait without hanging or panicking.

System tests were run locally, but some fail on both unpatched and patched binaries due to unrelated environment issues. Full `make validatepr` was not run.

Fixes #30090

comments.body: Thanks for the review @Luap99 . I updated the test based on your inline suggestions. This change releases the pod lock before the health wait, but it does not change waitForHealthy’s container-lock unlock/relock behavior or address the state-refresh concern you raised. I kept this PR focused on the pod-lock issue. Since you noted the concern isn’t blocking, I’ve left the broader rework out for now; let me know if you’d prefer it handled here.
